newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany says stance unchanged on Iran ambassador.
newsitem.headline: Germany says stance unchanged on Iran ambassador.

text.p: Germany's Foreign Ministry said on Sunday new initiatives to return European ambassadors to Tehran did not alter its understanding of current European Union policy on the issue.
Earlier, Iran's outgoing President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani indicated that ambassadors of European Union states may now return to Tehran, but Bonn's envoy must be the last.
A German Foreign Ministry spokesman said, however, that such comments did not alter Bonn's understanding of the current EU policy of keeping Tehran ambassadors at home.

"The Luxembourg (European Union) presidency has said it has tried to bring about the return of EU ambassadors to Tehran without discrimination and that this effort has failed. The ball is in Tehran's court," he said by telephone.

All EU states except for Greece recalled their ambassadors from Tehran after a German court concluded in April that Iran's top leaders had ordered the 1992 assassination of four Iranian Kurdish dissidents in a Berlin restaurant.

Iran and the EU have been engaged in last-minute efforts to try to get the EU's envoys back to Tehran in time for new president Mohammad Khatami's swearing-in ceremony in parliament on Monday, diplomats said on Sunday. REUTER
